summary: Reviewed 4 files (standalone-import.ts, index.ts, synthesis-parser.ts, ledger-store.ts archiveDocuments/importStandaloneProject). 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium. Two Low/Info observations noted. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A01/A04 — Path traversal (defense-in-depth): planFolderBasename() in path-validator.ts validates only the basename (last path segment) of the supplied project_path/cwd_path. A crafted input like '../../some/dir/2026-01-01-evil' passes the YYYY-MM-DD pattern check; path.join() then normalizes the traversal to an absolute path. In practice this is low risk: (1) path.join() normalizes the traversal, producing a predictable absolute path; (2) the tool only reads two specifically named files (plan.md, synthesis.md) and archives them — no shell execution, no secret exfiltration, no writes to the supplied path; (3) this is a local developer tool with developer-controlled inputs. Remediation (optional, defense-in-depth): add path.isAbsolute() assertion after receiving the input, rejecting non-absolute paths explicitly. Already partially mitigated: basename-only validation + path.join normalization limits the exploitable surface.

A04 — No length cap on outcomeSummary from synthesis.md: parseOutcomeSummary() returns the full body of the '### Outcome Summary' section with no truncation (standalone-import.ts line ~130, synthesis-parser.ts extractSection()). An abnormally large synthesis section would store equally large text in the wpDetail.pipelines[0].summary JSON field. For a developer-controlled local file this is acceptable, but a max-length guard (e.g. 4096 chars) would prevent unexpectedly large ledger records. Risk: Info-level — no security impact in normal operation.

All OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed — no Critical or High issues identified. A02 (no crypto ops, no secrets stored), A03 (no injection vectors: no SQL, no shell execution, no eval; outcomeSummary stored as JSON-serialized string), A05 (error messages expose filesystem paths supplied by the caller — acceptable and expected for a local developer MCP tool), A06 (no new dependencies added in this WP), A07 (MCP runs locally, no auth surface), A08 (JSON writes via atomicWriteJson within a write lock — no integrity gap), A09 (no audit log for import events — not expected at this tier), A10 (no HTTP/network requests made). Security sign-off confirmed.
